key_insight: A new chemically-grounded benchmark suite demonstrates how large language model capabilities scale and fall short across realistic small‑molecule drug design tasks, revealing strengths in representation and reasoning but clear gaps in reliable design and property prediction.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of realistic, chemistry-aware benchmarks for evaluating LLMs on end‑to‑end small‑molecule drug‑design workflows, bridging the gap between toy tasks and real-world discovery scenarios.
method: Curate a suite of chemically‑grounded tasks spanning molecular property prediction, molecular representation transformations (e.g., SMILES ⇄ IUPAC/name conversions), and molecular design challenges.
Formulate tasks as reinforcement‑style sequential decision problems to reflect multi‑step, real‑world workflows and to probe reasoning and planning capabilities.
Systematically evaluate multiple LLMs across these tasks, analyzing capability progression, failure modes, and where model improvements translate into practical utility.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners and drug‑discovery teams with a realistic benchmark and diagnostic toolkit to choose, tune, or develop LLMs for chemistry workflows, accelerating safe and effective integration of LLMs into molecule design pipelines.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing the benchmark suite: inputs (molecules, textual prompts) → task types (prediction, transformation, design) → outputs and evaluation metrics.
Radar chart comparing multiple LLMs across task categories (property prediction, representation conversion, design quality, robustness).
Before/after example of a molecule representation transformation (SMILES → IUPAC → canonical SMILES) or a scaffold modification produced by an LLM.
Heatmap of common failure modes (chemical validity, synthesizability, property mismatch) across models and tasks.
paper_title: Evaluating the Progression of Large Language Model Capabilities for Small-Molecule Drug Design
paper_authors: Shriram Chennakesavalu, Kirill Shmilovich, Hayley Weir, Colin Grambow, John Bradshaw
